name: University of Derby

settingEvidence.evidence: This is your chance to explore the campus and city, and experience what life could be like studying here.

fees.text: £9,790 per year for UK students starting in September 2026 or January 2027 (2026/27). Derby hasn't published a 2027/28 fee yet; fees are set by the UK government and may change each year.

source.evidence: For most undergraduate courses, if you start in September 2026 or January 2027, you will pay £9,790 per year.

livingCosts.text: University halls for undergraduates cost about £119–£208 a week in 2026/27: standard single rooms from £119.42, ensuites £150.57–£187.25, studios up to £207.76. Most contracts are 42 or 50 weeks; studios are 51 weeks.

source.evidence: Our premium standard rooms have been reduced from £140.56 to £128.59 a week, saving £500 on a typical 42-week contract.

openDays.text: Next open days: Sunday 8 November 2026, Saturday 5 December 2026 and Saturday 9 January 2027 (all 9:30am to 3:00pm). Later dates aren't listed yet; bookings open about two months before each one.

contextual.summary: Derby may lower the grades it asks for, or give extra consideration, to applicants who are care experienced, estranged from their families, refugees or asylum seekers, or whose parents/carers are in the UK armed forces.

criteria.detail: Students who are estranged from their families
Students who are refugees or asylum seekers
Students whose parents/carers are in the UK armed forces

contextual.rulesText: Typical criteria may include one or more of the listed groups, and students need to declare that they meet one of them on their application. Derby may either reduce grade requirements or give extra consideration when deciding whether to give a contextual offer; no grade reduction is published.

source.evidence: We will use the information in an application form and may either reduce grade requirements or give extra consideration when deciding whether to give a contextual offer.

programmes.name: Let's Get Down to Business
programmes.summary: A one-day event at Derby's Cavendish Building where Year 12 and 13 students try business sessions with academics and pitch a live business brief to a panel of business leaders and researchers.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 and 13 students. The page lists no other entry rules and doesn't say whether students book themselves or through their school or college.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Aimed at Year 12 and 13 students; no widening participation criteria are mentioned. Held at the Cavendish Building, Derby Campus, 1 Agard Street, Derby, DE1 1DZ, from 9:30am to 2:45pm.
benefits: Sessions led by Derby International Business School academics and current students
A live brief from one of Derby's industry links, pitched to a panel of business leaders and active researchers

runs.text: Wednesday 11 November 2026, 9:30am to 2:45pm; the event also runs on Wednesday 17 March 2027

opens.text: Bookings are open now for 11 November 2026; the booking form for 17 March 2027 goes live after the November event

notes: Derby shows its offers as UCAS tariff points (112 points on every course recorded) with the A-level grades alongside (BBC). The course pages list no required A-level subjects, only GCSE Maths and English at grade 4.
No 2028-entry requirements yet: Derby's course pages show typical requirements for September 2026 and September 2027 entry only, so 2027 entry is used for all courses.

Economics, Economics and Finance and the two joint honours Economics degrees are taught at Kedleston Road, Derby Campus (DE22 1GB). The Business Management courses are taught in the Cavendish Building, 1 Agard Street, Derby, DE1 1DZ (another Derby Campus site, nearer the city centre).
Derby is not on UAT-UK's TMUA list for 2027 entry and none of the course pages mention an admissions test.
The fees and finance page still quotes an older halls range of £115-157 a week; the dated 2026-27 halls price list (£119.42-£207.76) is used here.

Derby's Year 12-13 outreach activity guide mostly lists sessions booked through schools and colleges (workshops, EPQ information days, library visits); it has no Economics-specific Year 12 event. The Business and Management outreach page lists Let's Get Down to Business for Year 12.
